quotes.text: For each category, 30 harmful instructions were generated using GPT-4.1 (gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, temperature = 1.0)
The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.

rationale: Sources are named (generating model snapshot, an unnamed hospital database) but no dataset name, snapshot date or route from a task to its source record appears on S1-S3. The MIMIC-IV version and traceability statements exist only in S4 code comments, which never count (G1a).

quotes.text: This project is licensed under the MIT License.
For each category, 30 harmful instructions were generated using GPT-4.1 (gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, temperature = 1.0)

rationale: Origin, collection method and licence or terms are stated, but no consent or IRB status or explicit 'not required' appears on S1-S3; a data use agreement is not consent or IRB. The waiver-of-consent statement is only in an S4 code comment, which does not count.

quotes.text: The distribution of violated principles was uneven across the dataset.

rationale: Descriptive statistics of the dataset (principle distribution) and a stated sampling design (30 instructions per category, nine categories) are given. No comparison against a named target population is reported.

quotes.text: The mean violation rate across all models was 54.4%
Discriminatory Provision of Healthcare Services | DPH | Patient C is requesting water.

rationale: The whole benchmark is an unsafe-output test (violation rate over 270 harmful instructions). A dedicated discrimination category (DPH) tests bias-related compliance, so both test types are present.

quotes.text: A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces
every released task carries a canary string

rationale: A held-out split and canary string are reported (developer-side controls), but no measured contamination check appears on S1-S3. The verbatim-overlap measurement is only in an S4 code comment, which does not count.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment, so answers cannot leak through external search.
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces

rationale: Isolation from ground truth at run time is stated with named mechanisms (no web access, restricted retrieval, hidden labels not public).

quotes.text: The environment is frozen at release: the database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions
no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test

contradiction_quotes.text: no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test

rationale: Data, software and simulator are reported pinned with no external call other than the model under test, which meets the 2 anchor. The scoring code calls the OpenAI API for the judge (pinned snapshot but live service), a candidate contradiction of the no-external-service claim.

quotes.text: Solvability was confirmed by executing a scripted reference solution for every task through the grader.

rationale: A scripted reference solution was run through the grader for every task and the result (all 120 correct) is reported.

quotes.text: Grading validates both intended state modifications and preservation of unrelated records.

rationale: Tasks change state (skills such as modifyRemoteData, deleteRemoteData, toggleMachinePower), so NA does not apply. The grader is reported to check unchanged as well as changed state and to score unintended changes as failures.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks, and a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks.

rationale: Empirical do-nothing and random-agent rates are reported. A separate Appendix Z note gives a different random-action rate (3.1%) and says per-metric chance rates are in the appendix.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks, and a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks.

rationale: The do-nothing and random agent scores are reported for all 120 tasks.

quotes.text: The evaluator was validated against 200 physician-labeled outputs. Physician agreement reached 94%, with 3% false positives and 8% false negatives.

rationale: Own validation on 200 physician-labeled outputs with agreement and error figures is reported. The same chunk's limitation text says formal inter-rater assessment against human raters remains to be conducted, which is in tension with it; recorded as a note, not a score change.

quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed. The main text describes the policy of executing each task three times.

rationale: Temperature 0 and a fixed seed plus a repeated-run policy are stated in S1. The packet is inconsistent on the policy: another S1 sentence says five runs at temperature 0.7, and the methods describe one independent session per instruction at temperature 0.0.

quotes.text: Differences in violation rates between proprietary and open-weight models were assessed using a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test.

rationale: Tests are reported for headline comparisons (Kruskal-Wallis across families, Wilcoxon for proprietary vs open-weight, mixed-effects CIs in Table 3). Note: methods say two-sided but results say one-sided for the Wilcoxon test.

quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds
Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed.

rationale: Run count (five), seed and decoding policy, and independence of runs are all stated on S1. The packet conflicts on details (three vs five runs, temperature 0 vs 0.7), recorded as a note.

quotes.text: We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks, so the resampling unit is the task
where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering

rationale: CIs, the resampling unit (task) and clustering of tasks within patients are all stated on S1.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No agreement of actions or end state across reruns and no pass^k-type metric or per-task repeat outcome is reported; the only rerun mention is that scores are means over five runs, with no variation reported.

quotes.text: snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, with temperature 0
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0

rationale: Snapshot IDs, decoding parameters (and reasoning disabled) and a harness release matching the reported numbers are stated. Note: v1.2.0 does not appear among the S3 release tags (v1.0.0, v2.0.0), and these snapshot IDs differ from the model list in the main text; no S1/S4 mismatch for the same model role.

quotes.text: Each tool is defined by a JSON schema listing its name, arguments and argument types.
The documentation states for every tool whether it only reads or also writes state
These tool descriptions are included in the agent prompt.

rationale: Schema, read/write side effects per tool, and return semantics including error messages are all stated. S1 states the descriptions are in the agent prompt, though the agent prompt itself is not among the S5 chunks.

quotes.text: A mock server received the LLM’s response and returned a simulated execution acknowledgment

rationale: Simulated tool execution is disclosed on S1. No tests or conformance checks of the tools are reported, and nothing in the packet shows the simulation is disclosed in the agent-visible prompt.

quotes.text: A mock server received the LLM’s response and returned a simulated execution acknowledgment
Any unintended changes are caught and scored as failures.

rationale: Skills include write actions (modifyRemoteData, deleteRemoteData, toggleMachinePower) and tool documentation states read vs write per tool; writes are simulated via a mock server; unsafe and unintended writes are scored. S5 reach of the simulated-write disclosure cannot be told from the packet.

quotes.text: the sequence of invoked actions, was recorded for subsequent harmfulness evaluation
This design isolates the safety-relevant decision-making of the LLM from confounds introduced by low-level robot control.
The evaluator was validated against 200 physician-labeled outputs.

rationale: Grader input is an LLM judge over the interaction log and action sequence; the plan-level design rationale is given; and validation against 200 physician labels with FP and FN rates is reported. Element (ii) is only weakly supported, as the rationale justifies grading plans rather than the judge itself.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment, so answers cannot leak through external search.
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces
every released task carries a canary string

rationale: Leakage controls, a private held-out split with hidden labels, and a canary string are all reported on S1.

quotes.text: Accuracy is reported by task family (diagnosis, ordering, documentation) and by patient subgroup (sex, race)
with case counts displayed for every slice in the tables.

rationale: Results by task family and patient subgroup with case counts per slice are stated; the main results are also reported per harm category (30 instructions each).

quotes.text: The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.
Their use was approved under a data use agreement requiring credentialed access and de-identification by the safe harbour method
the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence

rationale: Source of records (real, de-identified), governance (DUA, credentialed access, safe-harbour de-identification) and data terms separate from the code licence are all stated on S1.
